summary: A 52-foot steel tower first built as a Michigan welcome-center ornament, moved to St. Ignace and lit as a marina light in 2006.

notes_for_editor: 1) Built year: the St. Ignace News and LighthouseFriends say Ed Morris built the tower in 1997; the Chamber of Commerce, Discover St. Ignace and (lead only) Wikipedia say 1998. The story states both. 2) Height (52 ft vs 54 ft) is now stated in the story: St. Ignace News 54 ft; Chamber and Discover St. Ignace 52 ft. Focal height: the record's 7.6 m is contradicted by the Coast Guard figure of 62 ft (18.9 m) to the focal plane, given by the Chamber; this is in corrections for human review. 3) Range: sources say 'more than 13 miles' (unit not stated; LighthouseFriends says 13.2 miles). The record's range_nm 13.0 may be statute miles (about 11.3 nm). Not corrected: needs the Coast Guard light list. 4) Record events '2006 built (Rowlett's Lighthouse Directory)' and '2010 built (Tower 2)' are not supported by any source read; check before publishing. 5) The corpus 'Wawatam' hits in the Life-Saving Service reports (1902-1909) and the Lighthouse Board volumes are the steamer Wawatam, not this light; not used. 6) The Coast Guard's own listing (USCG 7-12608) and the USLHS place record (which calls it a 'Private (Faux) Lighthouse') were not read in full; the USLHS roster is empty. 7) Lighthouse status: the Coast Guard describes it as an official aid, per the Chamber; no keepers. 8) Wikipedia is used for leads only; no fact rests on it.
